objections.title: conftest.py intra_city_routes:[] (array) contradicts schema type:object — BA did not flag as out_of_scope_observation
objections.description: tests/server/conftest.py:95 sets 'intra_city_routes': [] (a JSON array). schemas/v2/day.schema.json:71-88 defines intra_city_routes as type:object with string keys ('from_option_id:to_option_id:mode' format) and additionalProperties specifying a nested object shape. The fixture therefore fails schema validation on this field. BA's conftest.py component chain entry claims 'Synthetic trip data matches the v2 per-day-file schema' (conftest.py docstring). This is false for intra_city_routes. Furthermore, save.py:85 uses day.setdefault('intra_city_routes', []) and appends dicts as list items — also inconsistent with the schema's object shape. BA's scope (M7 conftest fix) only corrects slot path; it leaves intra_city_routes type wrong. BA did not record this as an out_of_scope_observation. Codex independently confirmed this gap.
objections.ba_claim: conftest.py fixture data matches the v2 per-day-file schema from schemas/v2/day.schema.json (docstring)
objections.actual_finding: conftest.py:95 intra_city_routes:[] is an array; schema line 72 requires type:object. Also save.py:85 uses setdefault('intra_city_routes',[]) treating it as a list. BA did not flag either.
objections.evidence: schemas/v2/day.schema.json:71-88 (type:object, additionalProperties:object); tests/server/conftest.py:95 ('[...]'); scripts/lib/server/save.py:85 ('day.setdefault("intra_city_routes", [])'); Codex output confirmed gap.
objections.recommended_fix: BA must add an out_of_scope_observation documenting the intra_city_routes type mismatch (array vs object) in conftest.py and save.py. AC7 must be updated to also require intra_city_routes:{} (empty object, not []) in the corrected fixture. If dev fixes slot path but leaves intra_city_routes:[] in the fixture, the day file written by the fixture will still fail schema validation. This must be explicit in the spec.

objections.title: test_save_endpoint.py:51 deterministically broken after Bug 1 fix — BA marks this as 'may need' instead of 'will break'
objections.description: tests/server/test_save_endpoint.py:51 reads 'slot = day.get("breakfast", {})' from the top-level day dict after calling handle_save(). Once Bug 1 is fixed, save.py will write breakfast under day["slots"]["breakfast"], not at day["breakfast"]. The top-level day.get("breakfast") will return {} (default), and the assertion 'slot.get("selected_option_id") == "breakfast-1-2"' will fail deterministically. BA's S1 says 'run pytest... and fix any assertion-path mismatches caused by the new slot layout' with 'may also need slot-path updates'. The word 'may' is incorrect — this test WILL break. BA's investigation_completeness is deficient here: BA read conftest.py but did not read test_save_endpoint.py:51 to confirm the breakage, leaving it hedged when it should be stated as certain. Codex independently confirmed 'test_save_endpoint.py:51 reads day["breakfast"]' as a confirmed break.
objections.ba_claim: tests/server/test_save_endpoint.py may also need slot-path updates but dev must confirm by running tests after conftest fix
objections.actual_finding: test_save_endpoint.py:51 'slot = day.get("breakfast", {})' is a top-level read that will deterministically return {} after the Bug 1 fix. test_save_endpoint.py:64 'day.get("stage")' is top-level and will still work (stage stays top-level). The slot assertion at line 52 will fail.
objections.evidence: tests/server/test_save_endpoint.py lines 50-52 read by QA; save.py Bug 1 fix moves slot write to day["slots"][breakfast"]; after fix, day.get("breakfast",{}) returns {}
objections.recommended_fix: BA must change S1 from 'may also need' to 'will need' slot-path updates, and move the test_save_endpoint.py fix into scope as a Must-Have (or clearly state it is tested by S1 and WILL fail without a fix). The AC7 verification should additionally confirm that test_save_endpoint assertions are updated to read from day["slots"][slot_id].

objections.title: Technical hint for StateMachineError import path uses wrong style for save.py
objections.description: BA's technical hint states: 'import in save.py via from scripts.lib.trip_contract.errors import StateMachineError (adjust import path to match existing project import style in save.py)'. The parenthetical caveat is contradictory: save.py uses relative imports exclusively (from .common import ...). The absolute path 'from scripts.lib.trip_contract.errors' is the wrong style. The correct pattern, consistent with save.py:18 ('from .common import ...') and the state_machine hint ('from lib.trip_contract.state_machine import validate_state_transition'), would be either 'from lib.trip_contract.errors import StateMachineError' (matching the serve-trip.py context path) or a relative import style. BA also did not specify that StateMachineError should subclass TripContractError (which Codex flagged as best practice to maintain exception hierarchy consistency).
objections.ba_claim: import in save.py via 'from scripts.lib.trip_contract.errors import StateMachineError' (adjust import path to match existing project import style)
objections.actual_finding: save.py uses 'from .common import ...' (relative imports). The absolute-path hint is wrong. Immediately below in the same spec, the state machine import hint correctly uses 'from lib.trip_contract.state_machine import validate_state_transition'. The inconsistency may confuse dev.
objections.evidence: scripts/lib/server/save.py:18 'from .common import (TripStore, ...)'; BA Technical Hints section, StateMachineError location bullet
objections.recommended_fix: Correct the import hint to 'from lib.trip_contract.errors import StateMachineError' (matching serve-trip.py's import context) or 'from .errors import StateMachineError' if importing within the same package (not applicable here since errors.py is in trip_contract, not server). Also add a note that StateMachineError should subclass TripContractError for hierarchy consistency.

objections.title: AC4 specifies 'server returns HTTP 409' but tests call handle_save() directly — no HTTP layer exercised
objections.description: AC4 states 'THEN the server returns HTTP 409 with body {"error": "state_machine", "detail": "<reason>"}'. The existing test infrastructure (test_save_endpoint.py) calls handle_save() directly without going through the HTTP dispatch layer in serve-trip.py. This means a unit test of handle_save() will NOT verify the HTTP 409 mapping in _handle_post_save(). The AC literally requires HTTP 409, which can only be verified by either (a) a test that instantiates TripServerHandler or uses a test client, or (b) by separately testing the serve-trip.py catch block. BA did not address this gap. A dev who writes a StateMachineError raise in save.py but omits the try/except in serve-trip.py will pass handle_save() unit tests but fail AC4. Codex flagged this as 'add/require a test for serve-trip.py exception-to-409 mapping'.
objections.ba_claim: AC4: server returns HTTP 409 (verifiable by test)
objections.actual_finding: Test infrastructure calls handle_save() directly; serve-trip.py _handle_post_save() is never invoked in existing tests. AC4 as written requires HTTP-layer verification that the existing test architecture cannot provide without adding serve-trip.py integration tests.
objections.evidence: tests/server/test_save_endpoint.py:1-4 'Tests call handle_save() directly. No HTTP port allocated.'; serve-trip.py:209-212 _handle_post_save() is the HTTP catch point
objections.recommended_fix: Either (a) update AC4 to specify 'handle_save() raises StateMachineError; _handle_post_save() catches it and returns HTTP 409 — verified by a new integration test or by reading serve-trip.py code post-fix', or (b) add to S1 or M5 a requirement to add a minimal HTTP-layer test. The spec must not leave the HTTP-409 mapping unverifiable.
